question.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $p$ is $4{p}^{2}=25.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and collect the like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{p}^{2} & =25 \\ 4{p}^{2}-25 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{p}^{2}-25 & =0 \\ (2p)^{2}-{5}^{2} & =0 \\ (2p-5)(2p+5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
2p-5=0\,\text{or}\,2p+5=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2p-5 & =0 & \, & \, & 2p+5 & =0 \\ 2p & =5 & \, & \, & 2p & =-5 \\ p & =\frac{5}{2} & \, & \, & p & =-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $p=-\frac{5}{2},\frac{5}{2}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $p=\pm \frac{5}{2}.$
